newsitem.title: USA: Tyson suspends Pine Bluff, Ark. poultry slaughter.
newsitem.headline: Tyson suspends Pine Bluff, Ark. poultry slaughter.

text.p: U.S. poultry producer Tyson Foods Inc has temporarily suspended slaughter operations at its Pine Bluff, Arkansas, facility, due to recent concern over dioxin levels, a company spokesman said.
"Operations at our Pine Bluff slaughter facility are currently not occurring," said Ed Nicholson, a Tyson spokesman.
Tyson's voluntary slaughter suspension began at midnight Sunday and will continue until dioxin levels fall to acceptable levels, Nicholson said.
The dioxin was traced to feed containing a clay ingredient that is sometimes used as a flowing or anti-caking agent in soymeal by some manufacturers.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food and Safety Inspection Service, in a notice to the livestock and poultry industry on July 8, ordered meat producers whose animals had been exposed to the feed to certify that dioxin levels met federal guidlines.
Producers must demonstrate that dioxin levels in meat from animals exposed to the feed do not exceed the federal limit of one part per trillion.
Less than one percent of U.S. livestock feed is affected, according to the FSIS.
"None of our plants that produce fresh chicken for the retail marketplace are among those affected by recent government actions," Tyson said in a statement.
The Pine Bluff facility produces 1.3 million chickens each week. Overall, Tyson produces 35 million broiler chickens weekly, Nicholson said.
